title: Every exception to the GSM Pause Delay must document the specific attack it enables
content:
The twelve pause-delay exceptions in A.1.10.3.2 share a template: what the bypass does, why it exists, and then a clause naming the harm it makes possible.

Executive Drop: "a malicious attacker may be able to delay or permanently block a legitimate governance proposal" (A.1.10.3.2.1). Oracle Freeze: oracles "may be frozen by an attacker in order to either: Prevent an expensive liquidation. Take advantage of a significant drop in collateral prices to mint unbacked USDS" (A.1.10.3.2.2). Direct Deposit Breaker: "a given line of USDS credit is unexpectedly shut down" (A.1.10.3.2.5). Dynamic Debt Ceiling: "a theoretical griefing attack on the IAM that prevents debt from being accessible" (A.1.10.3.2.6). The SP-BEAM, stUSDS BEAM and SBE-BEAM exceptions each name "malicious action by whitelisted operators" (A.1.10.3.2.10.2 to .10.4). Even a side effect is disclosed: triggering SPLITTER_MOM "also disables these rewards until the activation is reversed" (A.1.10.3.2.8).

The discipline is the notable thing, not any individual entry. Emergency powers are normally documented by their justification alone — the crisis they answer — because that is the persuasive part. Requiring the enabled attack to be written down alongside converts each exception into an explicit trade whose cost is on the record and can be revisited.

It also produces a usable artifact: read together, these clauses are a catalogue of Sky's fast-path attack surface, written by Sky. An attacker's shortlist and the defenders' shortlist are the same document, which is a deliberate bet that visibility helps defenders more than attackers.

Each exception's mitigation is named too — bounded parameters, a paired MOM contract, locked time — so the record is a trade rather than a confession.
description: Across A.1.10.3.2.1 to .12 each bypass carries a 'risk opened up by this exceptional functionality' clause, making the cost of each emergency power part of the Atlas record.
